key_insight: Graph grounding reduced hallucinations across all evaluated LLMs, while general-purpose models generally outperformed domain-specific models on complex reasoning.
clinical_relevance: Combining LLMs with structured biomedical knowledge may improve research tools relevant to medicine, but this benchmark does not establish clinical safety or effectiveness.
method: Benchmarked GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, and BioGPT.
Evaluated multitier queries across DrugBank, NeuroSynth, Cognitive Atlas, Brain Map, and GDPKG.
Compared graph-grounded and graph-agnostic reasoning and factual accuracy.
evidence_signal: Performance declined as query complexity increased; annotation agreement was substantial, with Cohen’s kappa of 0.781 and Fleiss’ kappa of 0.77.
watch_item: The abstract provides no dataset size or quantitative hallucination reductions, limiting assessment of effect magnitude and generalizability.
paper_title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
